summary: Quiet long-lived streams from tenant causing gradual dedicated-pool GPU squeeze in us-west
description: Issue summary: NimbusData (dedicated) reported a gradual throughput decline and rising p99 latency for batched text-generation routes in us-west starting ~2026-03-13 09:00 UTC. Impact: elevated p50->p99 latency (p99 from 320ms -> 1.8s) and reduced sustained throughput for their dedicated pool; customer reports periodic 429s and request queueing. Environment: prod dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-usw-34), models: redwood-14b-q4 and redwood-7b-quant. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run sustained harmony-like workload with many long-lived streaming connections and infrequent small inference bursts. 2) Observe allocator slot utilization and sustained KV prefetch growth. 3) Notice autoscaler did not add capacity; p99 climbs and requests queue. Observed logs/metrics: - allocator: many CONN_KEEPALIVE sessions from tenant (conn count ~4.3k) with idle_cpu but pinned GPU contexts. - prefetcher: KV cache growth for tenant up ~3.2x over 6 hours causing memory pressure. - nvme/io wait spikes coincident with nightly snapshotter job in the same reserved pool host set. - autoscaler telemetry indicates eligibility but attach failures due to "slot_unavailable" and "prefetch_backpressure". - tail traces show long-lived streams holding GPU slots via inactive but attached handles. Immediate impact: customer QPS dropped ~22% at peak window, backlog grew to ~150 pending batched requests. This is customer-impacting; remediation requested.
comments: 2026-03-13 10:05 - Support (Aisha Kaur): Raised ticket after initial triage call with NimbusData. Gathered request ids and example request traces. Customer confirms only their traffic uses this dedicated pool.

2026-03-13 11:30 - SRE (Evan Martinez): Observed large number of long-lived keepalive connections from tenant-origin IP range. Allocator logs show repeated attach attempts followed by handle retention. Correlates with prefetch growth. Taking snapshot of allocator state (s3://redwood-dumps/ded-usw-34/alloc-snap-2026-03-13-11:30).

2026-03-13 13:12 - Customer (NimbusData - Sarah Li): Noted they started a background monitoring agent yesterday that opens persistent streams to monitor latency; they did not expect streams to retain GPU contexts. Will attempt to throttle keepalives on their side.

2026-03-13 15:00 - Infra (Priya Shah): Confirmed nvme IO spike from snapshotter job on host-subset A; scheduled to re-run nightly. Snapshotter team to patch IO rate limit. Created INT-900101 for snapshotter rate-limiting work.

2026-03-14 08:20 - SRE (Evan Martinez): Applied temporary mitigation - enforced per-tenant connection cap (conn_limit=1500) and reduced prefetch window (max_prefetch_entries=5000) for pool ded-usw-34. Observed p99 drop from 1.8s -> 420ms and backlog clearing over 12 minutes. Notified customer of temporary config change.
2026-03-14 09:05 - Customer (Sarah Li): Confirms latency returned to acceptable range for current workload, asking for durable fix and recommended client-side changes.

2026-03-14 12:00 - Product (Liam O'Connor): Recommends follow-up: permanent per-tenant guardrails, heartbeat compression, and prefetch caps; evaluate autoscaler sensitivity to prefetch-driven memory pressure. Linked PRs for allocator and prefetcher noted above.
investigation: Hypothesis: long-lived low-throughput streams from a single tenant were holding GPU handles and growing per-tenant KV prefetch state; combined with an unthrottled snapshotter IO job on the same host subpool, this produced slot unavailability and prevented autoscaler from reconciling attachments. Evidence: allocator handles list contained ~3.9k 'attached' entries for tenant NIM-42 where last_active_ts is > 2h but last_cpu_ms is low; prefetcher metrics show uneven growth only for tenant; host io wait spikes align with snapshot window; after applying connection cap, recovered latency and throughput. Alternative explanations considered: kernel-level driver issue, model-specific kernel regression — ruled out because other tenants on the same pool unaffected and model kernel metrics normal.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: enforced per-tenant connection cap and reduced prefetch window for ded-usw-34 (applied 2026-03-14 08:20). Scheduled snapshotter IO rate-limit patch (INT-900101). Workarounds for customer: - Rapid: implement client-side connection pooling to avoid thousands of persistent streams; add exponential backoff for monitoring agent. - Medium: enable client heartbeat compression (recommended flag) and limit client-side prefetch hints. Permanent plan: 1) Add allocator-side per-tenant soft and hard resource guardrails (conn_cap, prefetch_cap) across Dedicated pools (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/3821). 2) Autoscaler tuning to consider prefetch memory signal when computing desired capacity. 3) Run a fairness sweep for reserved pools to detect tenants with disproportionate handle retention. Postmortem and runbook updates: updated Confluence runbook and recommended customer onboarding checklist for dedicated pools (pages linked above). Follow-ups: - SRE to monitor ded-usw-34 for 72 hours (assignee: Evan Martinez). - Product to schedule allocator hardening in next sprint (owner: Liam O'Connor). - Customer success to review NimbusData's integration and recommend client changes (owner: Priya Shah).
